themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch behavior from the outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On provable downstream consent and deletion all three models said opaque ad platforms and already-trained models expose no lineage or deletion evidence, with Gemini calling proof of removed influence mathematically impossible without retraining, and the same wall appears in agentic traffic, incrementality, and the B2B buying-group problem where decisions happen in private channels.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often changes while you measure it. So the models keep starting by building a small truth set of their own, or by admitting the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: In answer engine optimization Claude said the instrument drifts more than the effect being measured, in identity resolution nobody has truth about who is the same person, in the B2B intent problem a degraded signal and a signal that was never real look identical, and in content review expert reviewers disagree with each other.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: All three models answered safe agent execution with a proxy or gateway in front of every write and hard caps on spend and audience size, and today all three answered downstream consent by inventorying every path data leaves and putting a single checkpoint or expiring feed in front of it.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the person holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The models increasingly try to make honesty pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic all three proposed a fast lane or price perk so declaring beats spoofing, on journey orchestration they named channel bonuses that reward saying yes, on the semantic context layer they called conflicting definitions a political settlement, and on downstream consent Gemini said partners are structurally incentivized to stay black boxes.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it: generate only from pre-approved claims, and accept that a person still decides the edge cases.
themes.evidence: On governance of generative content all three models built an approved-claim registry tied to evidence and constrained generation to it, while agreeing that deciding whether creative framing breaks a claim stays a human judgment, and the semantic context layer answers make the same point about the meaning of "customer".
